purpose: Prove by combinatorial policy arithmetic that 600 routine_volume matters can share realistic public structures without collapsing into duplicate combined semantic signatures. No cases are generated.
claim: Shared MG/public forms, layouts, defence positions and stages are expected; uniqueness is carried by substantive combinations, not by IDs/salts/cosmetic wording.

documentGraphSharing.note: Many routine packs can share the same document-existence graph.

combinatorialLowerBound.method: Conservative product using only a subset of axes with reduced cardinalities to avoid overclaim.
combinatorialLowerBound.implication: Even under reduced cardinalities, available substantive combinations >> 600, so routine matters need not invent ID/salt/cosmetic uniqueness.
combinatorialLowerBound.withSharedPublicForms: Holding publicFormStructure fixed still leaves 165888 combinations across the nine axes.

nonCollapseGuarantees: Combined semantic signature target unique rate = 1.0 within routine_volume.
Combined signature dominance cap = 0.5% (max cluster 3) as fail-closed brake only.
Cosmetic uniqueness rejection detector blocks manufactured diversity.
Document/evidence graph clustering within caps does not alone satisfy uniqueness.
explicitlyNotProvenHere: Actual selection or generation of 600 matters
Empirical cluster histograms from a membership
validationHooks: When routine_volume membership exists: report shared form repetition counts (informational).
Assert combinedSemanticSignature unique rate == 1.0 for the 600.
Assert cosmetic detector reject count for accepted members == 0.
